subject: 🏃 Sunday — Bay to Breakers 15K (Wk 2)
html:
Tomorrow: Bay to Breakers 15K — your first race-effort workout of the V6 plan. 10 miles total. Miles 1–6 at 8:30–8:45 steady (HR 140–155), then miles 6–9.3 at marathon pace 7:35–7:45. Hard cap at 7:35 — do not let race-day adrenaline pull you under. Hayes Hill at mile 2: run it by effort, not pace. Let the watch float and stay conversational on the climb.

Pre-run activation (5 min before corral): Hip CARs, banded lateral walks, glute bridges, plus quadruped banded hip IR 5–10 reps each side. Keep it light — you're warming up, not training.

Fuel (PF30 — Maurten didn't arrive, switched yesterday): Oatmeal + banana 60 min pre-start (~50–60g carbs). 2 × Precision Fuel PF30 gels — mile 3 and mile 5.5. The mile-5.5 gel lands before the MP surge at mile 6, avoiding a stitch at the effort transition. That's 60g over ~80 min (≈45 g/hr). Half LMNT packet in your 14oz handheld (500mg sodium) — sip between aid stations, take water at every one.

Knee veto (still active): If you wake up tomorrow at 2+ on the 5-point scale, run the entire 10 mi easy at 9:00 and skip the fast finish. You've been 1/5 across every session this week — track VO2, heavy squat, threshold progression, bodyweight stability, and today's bike ride — so the veto is unlikely, but the rule stands.

Focus cue: Patience through mile 6. The steady miles are not junk — they're building the aerobic base for the MP finish. When you flip to 7:35–7:45, it should feel like releasing a coiled spring, not grinding from the start. If HR is already 160+ at mile 5, hold steady pace through the finish instead.

Context: Week 2 of 12, Phase 1 Foundation. This is your first fast-finish stimulus and the first race-day fuel rehearsal with PF30. The data feeds directly into the May 30 PAL 10K calibration and the Week 7 Presidio Pivot test. 10 weeks to SF Marathon.

Tonight: Hydrate, bed by 10. Lay out race kit, bib, handheld, gels. Set alarm with time for oatmeal 60 min before start. You're ready — the week has been clean.
